artifacts.name: candidate-runtime-trust-correction-r17.md
artifacts.content:
# Revision 17 Redesign Route

All 19 declared context sources authenticated against their exact byte counts and SHA-256 digests before implementation began. No repository files, evidence, package metadata, or Git state were modified.

The approved four-file scope cannot close the release-review trust chain. The live harness and verifier remain circular self-authentication roots; repository-local materialization permits ancestor dependency resolution; copying installed package directories does not prove lockfile SRI integrity; and fresh-child execution plus staged-output verification requires a separately trusted host bootstrap outside the candidate-controlled runtime.

Revision 17 must therefore be retired with outcome `redesign` and replaced by a wider, independently reviewed contract.

risks: Continuing within the approved scope would create release evidence whose trust root remains candidate-controlled or repository-live.
Repository-local runtime construction can resolve dependencies through ancestor node_modules.
Copied installed package bytes alone do not establish correspondence with lockfile integrity metadata.
followUps: Replan around a candidate-authenticated parent bootstrap outside the candidate-controlled runtime.
Materialize the complete candidate outside repository ancestry.
Install exact locked dependencies with npm ci --offline --ignore-scripts from an explicitly bound cache.
Execute candidate tooling in a fresh child process using only the private dependency supply.
Hash source, dependency, and generated closures before and after execution, then verify bounded cleanup.
Stage outputs privately and promote them only after parent-side verification.
Bind a direct runtimeBindingDigest into every release manifest, approval, package, handoff-verification report, and related evidence.
